description: Voting Village focuses on the cybersecurity, physical integrity, and policy challenges of election infrastructure, voting machines, and ballot return systems. Talks address vulnerabilities in electronic voting applications, vote-by-mail security, foreign influence operations, and federal coordination to safeguard democratic elections.

talks.title: Hacking Democracy II: On Securing an Election
talks.teaser: Convenes a panel to examine emerging cyber threats, disinformation campaigns, and coordinated vulnerability disclosure ahead of the 2020 election.
talks.summary:
Assessing Threats to Democratic Elections

Four years after the 2016 Presidential Election exposed fundamental vulnerabilities in election infrastructure, securing democratic processes requires continuous adaptation across technology, policy, and human factors.

Threat Modeling the 2020 Vote

The panel examines primary threat vectors targeting the 2020 election cycle, including foreign influence campaigns, targeted disinformation, web application tampering, and voting machine software vulnerabilities.

The Role of Hackers and Coordinated Disclosure

Independent cybersecurity researchers and coordinated vulnerability disclosure programs play a pivotal role in identifying flaws in voting infrastructure and building cyber-resilience across local jurisdictions.

Adapting Election Security During a Pandemic

The sudden shift toward remote and mail-in voting spurred by the COVID-19 pandemic introduced complex logistical hurdles, legal challenges, and rapid infrastructural expansions in the final ninety days before the election.

talks.title: How Influence Warfare Subverts Democracy
talks.teaser: Analyzes modern information warfare campaigns in Poland and Taiwan to forecast authoritarian influence tactics targeting democratic elections.
talks.summary:
Information Warfare as an Election Attack Vector

Modern authoritarian regimes increasingly deploy sophisticated information warfare and narrative manipulation campaigns to exploit social divisions and subvert democratic electorates.

Case Studies from Poland and Taiwan

Empirical research on influence operations conducted during recent elections in Poland and Taiwan reveals the tactical breadth of state-sponsored narrative injection and coordinated bot networks.

Foreshadowing Tactics for Presidential Elections

The influence methodologies refined in foreign operational theaters provide clear indicators of the disinformation playbooks deployed against the United States presidential election.

talks.title: Security Challenges Posed by State-Level Election Management Systems
talks.teaser: Examines cybersecurity challenges, SQL injection risks, and systemic vulnerabilities across state-level election management systems.
talks.summary:
John Odom examines the architectural vulnerabilities and cybersecurity risks inherent in state-level Election Management Systems (EMS) and voter registration databases. He highlights how the centralization of voter records into online portals creates high-value targets for both state-sponsored actors and cybercriminals.

Odom reviews known security vulnerabilities affecting state election websites and vendor infrastructure at 04:02 and 05:55. He analyzes attack vectors including SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and unauthorized database access at 08:02 and 10:11, illustrating how flawed validation logic could allow attackers to manipulate voter records, alter registration statuses, or disrupt poll operations on election day. He concludes with recommendations for independent security audits and mandatory defense-in-depth measures.

talks.title: Hack a Fax
talks.teaser: Demonstrates the lack of security in email and fax ballot return systems used by overseas voters and advocates for robust federal standards.
talks.summary:
Overseas Ballot Return Insecurities

Millions of military and overseas voters rely on electronic transmission methods, including email and facsimile, to return completed ballots under disparate state election statutes.

The Hack a Fax Demonstration

The National Cybersecurity Center developed a demonstration showing how unencrypted fax protocols and internet-to-fax gateways can be intercepted, altered, or blocked in transit.

Balancing Voter Accessibility with Security

While expanding ballot access for citizens living abroad is vital, relying on legacy protocols devoid of cryptographic verification introduces vulnerabilities that compromise election integrity.

Establishing Federal Standards for Electronic Ballot Return

Advocating for unified federal security standards ensures that modern ballot delivery and return platforms incorporate verifiable audit trails and end-to-end encryption.

talks.title: Remote Online Balloting Delivery
talks.teaser: Compares client-side and server-side architectures for remote ballot marking and analyzes their security and privacy risks.
talks.summary:
Remote Electronic Ballot Delivery During Pandemics

Election administrators increasingly deploy digital delivery systems to provide blank ballots to absentee voters and ensure accessible ballot marking for voters with disabilities.

Server-Side Versus Client-Side Marking Architectures

Remote ballot marking platforms diverge into systems that process selections on a remote cloud server and those that operate statelessly on the voter's local client device.

Security and Privacy Risk Profiles

Server-side marking introduces critical attack surfaces, including voter surveillance, ballot manipulation, and man-in-the-middle tampering by hosting providers or malicious actors.

Architectural Recommendations for Accessible Balloting

Mitigating privacy and integrity risks requires adopting stateless client-side rendering and printing physical paper ballots for postal return or secure drop box submission.

talks.title: Election Administration and Security in Washington State
talks.teaser: Washington Secretary of State Kim Wyman discusses vote-by-mail administration, physical and digital safeguards, and decentralized election security.
talks.summary:
Washington Secretary of State Kim Wyman and Communications Director Kylee Zabel address the DEF CON Voting Village on the operational administration, physical safeguards, and cybersecurity measures protecting Washington State's universal vote-by-mail election infrastructure [00:02]. With Washington operating entirely by mail for over a decade, Secretary Wyman shares lessons on administering secure, transparent, and accessible statewide elections during a presidential election year compounded by the COVID-19 pandemic [04:49].

Wyman outlines the "three-legged stool" framework supporting election integrity in Washington: physical security, process security, and digital cybersecurity [14:27]. She details physical chain-of-custody controls, including numbered tamper-evident seals on ballot drop boxes, continuous video monitoring, and bipartisan ballot transport teams [09:40]. Process security involves rigorous signature verification matching ballot return envelopes against voter registration records, paired with public reconciliation audits [09:40].

On the digital front, Wyman describes the modernization and architectural segmentation of Washington's voter database (VoteWA), explaining how network isolation, multi-factor authentication, and partnership with CISA, the FBI, and the National Guard ensure election system resilience [14:27]. She discusses administrative hurdles, including USPS operational concerns, federal funding needs, and strategies for debunking election misinformation [19:02, 26:23].

talks.title: Protecting Elections with Data Science
talks.teaser: Presents open-source data science tools designed to consolidate election results rapidly and detect reporting anomalies.
talks.summary:
Data Science Applications in Election Verification

Applying data science and statistical analysis to precinct-level returns enables election officials and watchdog groups to verify reporting consistency and identify systemic anomalies.

Consolidating Multi-Jurisdictional Results

An open-source consolidation tool aggregates fragmented reporting feeds from disparate voting machines and county databases into standardized data structures for audit verification.

Public-Facing Election Verification Portals

Deploying transparent web dashboards allows independent researchers and the public to monitor vote consolidation in real time, building confidence in official election outcomes.

talks.summary:
Social Engineering and Human-Oriented Security

This presentation explores social engineering attacks and human vulnerability in security systems. Topics include psychological manipulation, pretexting, credential harvesting, phishing techniques, and how attackers exploit human nature to bypass technical defenses in organizations.

talks.title: Analysis of Data from Mobile Voting Pilots
talks.teaser: Shares empirical attack telemetry and threat vector data collected across real-world smartphone mobile voting pilot deployments.
talks.summary:
Telemetry from Live Mobile Voting Pilots

Deploying mobile smartphone voting applications in pilot jurisdictions across the United States generated extensive telemetry on remote attack attempts and malicious probing.

Empirical Threat Vector Analysis

Analysis of collected telemetry categorizes attacks by geographic origin, duration, and lethality, detailing coordinated attempts to compromise client devices and backend application APIs.

Evaluating Defensive Mitigations

Comparing successful and unsuccessful defensive countermeasures highlights the effectiveness of rate limiting, client attestation, and API shielding against automated vulnerability scanning.

Public Release of Anonymized Attack Datasets

Publishing anonymized threat data in the public domain provides independent election researchers with empirical baselines to study adversary tradecraft targeting mobile ballot return platforms.

talks.title: A Lawyer's Reflections on Elections
talks.teaser: Examines elections as vulnerable human information systems through the lens of election litigation and administrative procedural failures.
talks.summary:
Elections as Fragile Information Systems

Local elections function fundamentally as complex information processing networks, rendering them susceptible to both malicious tampering and negligent human procedural failures.

Lessons from Municipal Election Litigation

Insights drawn from election lawsuit Delgadillo v. City of Peoria illustrate how statutory ambiguities and ballot counting errors create legal and operational impasses.

Overlooked Administrative and Procedural Flaws

Election challenges frequently center on systemic procedural vulnerabilities that administrators dismiss as minor, yet collectively distort local election outcomes.

Strengthening Legal and Operational Frameworks

Securing democratic governance requires harmonizing legal remedies with rigorous technical audit standards across municipal election jurisdictions.

talks.title: Remarks from Senator Ron Wyden
talks.teaser: U.S. Senator Ron Wyden discusses federal legislative efforts to mandate hand-marked paper ballots and post-election risk-limiting audits.
talks.summary:
United States Senator Ron Wyden of Oregon addresses the DEF CON Voting Village, emphasizing the paramount importance of securing American election infrastructure against foreign and domestic cyber threats. He commends the independent hacker community and Voting Village researchers for their patriotic work in exposing severe vulnerabilities in commercial voting machines and election management software.

Senator Wyden calls for urgent federal legislative action to mandate voter-verified hand-marked paper ballots across all jurisdictions, ban paperless direct-recording electronic (DRE) voting systems, and institute mandatory post-election risk-limiting audits. He stresses the necessity of holding commercial voting machine vendors accountable to rigorous, enforceable federal cybersecurity standards rather than voluntary guidelines.

talks.title: Remarks from the U.S. Election Assistance Commission
talks.teaser: U.S. Election Assistance Commission Chairman Benjamin Hovland discusses federal election assistance, funding, and election official support.
talks.summary:
Benjamin Hovland, Chairman of the U.S. Election Assistance Commission (EAC), delivers keynote remarks to the DEF CON Voting Village detailing federal initiatives to secure the 2020 presidential election amid the COVID-19 pandemic [00:00]. Hovland outlines the mission of the bipartisan EAC as the federal clearinghouse for voting system testing, certification standards, and grant administration for state and local election jurisdictions [03:30].

Hovland highlights the Rapid Architecture-Based Election Technology Verification (RABBIT) program, an innovative EAC initiative designed to provide agile security testing and verification for non-voting-machine election technology, such as electronic pollbooks, election night reporting (ENR) websites, and electronic ballot delivery systems [06:48]. He notes positive cultural shifts among commercial voting equipment manufacturers, who are increasingly embracing coordinated vulnerability disclosure programs, threat intelligence sharing, and formal bug bounties with security researchers [10:16].

The presentation emphasizes the critical role of the independent security research community in auditing election systems and identifying technical flaws before adversaries can exploit them [13:35]. Hovland concludes by addressing the severe shortage of poll workers caused by the pandemic, issuing a call for tech-savvy DEF CON attendees to volunteer as election workers to support secure and fair voting operations [16:52].

talks.title: The Ballot is Busted before the Blockchain
talks.teaser: Discloses reverse engineering findings and side-channel vulnerabilities in the Voatz blockchain mobile voting application.
talks.summary:
Security Analysis of the Voatz Mobile Voting App

In 2018, West Virginia deployed the Voatz mobile phone application for select overseas voters, asserting that permissioned blockchains, biometrics, and mixnets guaranteed ballot integrity.

Reverse Engineering and Cleanroom Server Reimplementation

Researchers reverse-engineered the compiled Android application and implemented a cleanroom server to dissect the proprietary protocol and client verification mechanisms.

Passive Side-Channel Secret Ballot Extraction

Security flaws enable a completely passive network eavesdropper to observe packet lengths and timing characteristics to accurately recover a voter's secret ballot selections.

Vulnerabilities in Third-Party Software Dependencies

The integration of commercial third-party SDKs for analytics and crash reporting exposes sensitive voter data and introduces critical points of failure into the voting pipeline.

talks.title: Secure the Vote Standards
talks.teaser: Presents draft security guidelines modeled after the VVSG to establish federal standards for electronic ballot return platforms.
talks.summary:
Emergence of Electronic Ballot Return Systems

The development of electronic ballot return solutions expands voting accessibility for overseas and disabled voters while introducing severe cybersecurity concerns into election systems.

Absence of Proactive Federal Guidance

The lack of binding federal architectural guidance leaves commercial developers without standardized security frameworks tailored specifically to election assurance.

The National Cybersecurity Center Guidelines

Security experts from the National Cybersecurity Center drafted baseline cybersecurity criteria modeled on the EAC Voluntary Voting System Guidelines (VVSG) for electronic ballot return.

Establishing Resilient Election Standards

Formally adopting verifiable security standards ensures that electronic ballot return platforms enforce rigorous auditability, data integrity, and vulnerability testing.

talks.title: Testing Can't Tell If Ballot Devices Alter Elections
talks.teaser: Demonstrates mathematical limitations showing that pre- and post-election logic and accuracy testing cannot prove ballot-marking devices did not alter votes.
talks.summary:
Election Security and Voting Systems

This talk addresses security challenges in voting systems and election infrastructure. The presentation discusses vulnerabilities in voting machines, ballot-handling systems, election administration software, and policy implications for maintaining electoral integrity and voter privacy.

talks.title: Policy Approach to Resolving Cybersecurity Problems
talks.teaser: Proposes a comprehensive federal policy approach to mandate vendor transparency, security standards, and cyber risk assessments in elections.
talks.summary:
Persistent Vulnerabilities in Voting Systems

Independent security researchers consistently identify critical vulnerabilities in voting machines, registration databases, and tabulation infrastructure without seeing meaningful vendor remediation.

Private Sector Vendor Unresponsiveness

Commercial election technology vendors frequently resist vulnerability disclosures and fail to demonstrate robust cybersecurity hygiene or adherence to recognized industry baselines.

Federal Policy Interventions for Election Integrity

Addressing market failures in voting system security requires federal policy mandates requiring regular third-party risk assessments and continuous vulnerability reporting.

Enforcing Accountability Across Voting Supply Chains

Establishing statutory vendor accountability ensures that manufacturers of voter registration platforms and tabulation hardware prioritize security fixes to protect democratic processes.

talks.title: Leveraging Electronic Balloting Options in COVID
talks.teaser: Shares insights from CISA on managing new attack surfaces and security trade-offs introduced by rapid shifts to electronic and absentee balloting.
talks.summary:
Pandemic Impacts on American Voting Infrastructure

The COVID-19 pandemic forced rapid structural transformations across U.S. elections, including massive shifts toward mail-in voting, consolidated polling places, and staffing shortages.

Emerging Attack Surfaces in Expanded Systems

Rapidly scaling online ballot request portals, postal ballot tracking software, and remote processing facilities introduced new potential points of failure and targeted disruption.

CISA Election Infrastructure Security Strategy

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) worked closely with state and local election officials to evaluate risk profiles and provide technical mitigation guidance.

Preserving Public Credibility in Election Outcomes

Safeguarding the integrity of pandemic-adapted voting systems requires transparent administrative procedures, multi-factor authentication, and resilient audit infrastructure.

talks.title: Don't Go Postal
talks.teaser: Offers actionable fixes and process improvements for vendors and state governments to secure vote-by-mail systems and registration.
talks.summary:
Vulnerabilities in Mail-In Voting Infrastructure

As election administrators shifted heavily toward mail-in voting, new operational vulnerabilities emerged spanning voter registration databases, ballot printing, and postal chain-of-custody.

Actionable Security Solutions for State Governments

Rather than merely documenting flaws, state agencies and voting equipment vendors can implement straightforward administrative and cryptographic safeguards to protect mailed ballots.

Securing the Voter Registration Lifecycle

Harden voter registration portals and mail ballot request pipelines by deploying robust identity verification, automated voter notifications, and rate-limited backend interfaces.

Practical Protections for Complex Election Systems

Adopting transparent tracking barcodes and standardized chain-of-custody verification ensures resilient vote-by-mail processes while maintaining broad democratic access.

talks.title: A Panel with the Feds on Election Security
talks.teaser: Features federal election security leaders discussing military Defend Forward strategies, state coordination, and countering disinformation.
talks.summary:
Federal Coordination in Election Infrastructure Defense

Federal security leaders review government initiatives since 2016 to coordinate threat intelligence sharing with state, local, and territorial election administrators.

The Military Defend Forward Strategy

U.S. Cyber Command and military intelligence agencies deploy the Defend Forward doctrine to disrupt foreign adversary infrastructure and counter election interference before it reaches domestic networks.

Countering Foreign and Domestic Disinformation

Federal inter-agency task forces manage foreign influence operations, track coordinated inauthentic behavior online, and provide transparent public corrections to preserve election integrity.

Partnering with the Hacker Community

The panel underscores actionable avenues for independent cybersecurity researchers to report vulnerabilities directly to federal agencies and assist in hardening election systems.

talks.title: A Panel with the Feds on Election Security Introduction

talks.summary:
This introductory segment introduces the marquee "Panel with the Feds on Election Security" in the DEF CON 28 Safe Mode Voting Village, presenting the professional backgrounds of federal officials and cybersecurity leaders convening to discuss the defense of the 2020 U.S. elections [00:11].

The introduction profiles panel participants: David Bordino (National Security Agency Election Security Lead), Brigadier General William Hartman (Commander, Cyber National Mission Force, U.S. Cyber Command), Matt Masterson (Senior Cybersecurity Advisor, Department of Homeland Security CISA), Cynthia Kaiser (Deputy Chief of Analysis for National Security Cyber Threats, FBI), Maurice Turner (Senior Advisor, U.S. Election Assistance Commission), and panel moderator Bryson Bort (Founder of SCYTHE and GRIMM, and Co-Founder of the ICS Village) [00:25]. The bios underscore the cross-agency collaboration between intelligence, military, law enforcement, and civil election administrators in mitigating foreign threat actor interference in American democratic processes.

talks.title: Review of Remote Voting in Response to COVID-19
talks.teaser: Sang Oun Lee presents an evaluation framework assessing the trustworthiness and security of remote voting methods during pandemic conditions, drawing lessons from South Korea.
talks.summary:
Evaluating Remote Voting Amidst Public Health Crises

Global pandemic containment measures forced election administrators worldwide to evaluate alternative remote voting modalities—including vote-by-mail, online voting, and blockchain-based solutions.

An Objective Framework for Election Security Evaluation

Sang Oun Lee introduces an evaluation methodology to assess the trustworthiness, voter anonymity, and auditability of remote balloting procedures under emergency constraints.

Case Study: South Korea's Pandemic General Election

Lee analyzes the Republic of Korea's April 2020 national legislative elections, which achieved record voter turnout during an active epidemic through strict biometric and hygienic protocols without compromising ballot integrity.

Policy Guidance for Election Administrators

The presentation outlines policy recommendations for local election jurisdictions, balancing public health necessity against the imperative of verifiable voter authentication and chain of custody.

talks.title: Heightened Election Security Risks Amidst a Pandemic
talks.teaser: CISA election security advisors Jack Cable and Alex Zaheer analyze emerging threat vectors and infrastructure attack surfaces resulting from the rapid shift to remote voting.
talks.summary:
Pandemic-Driven Transformations in Election Operations

The COVID-19 pandemic necessitated an unprecedented shift toward mail-in balloting, consolidated in-person polling facilities, and emergency budget reallocations across thousands of U.S. election jurisdictions.

Expanding Threat Surfaces in State and Local Infrastructure

CISA advisors Jack Cable and Alex Zaheer explore how hastily expanded online voter registration portals, automated ballot processing systems, and third-party logistics vendors created new technical attack surfaces.

Federal Coordination and Technical Assistance

The speakers detail CISA's operational support framework, offering vulnerability scanning, cyber hygiene evaluations, and incident response coordination to local election officials.

Building Public Confidence in Democratic Integrity

The authors emphasize defensive validation, paper-based audit trails, and transparent risk communications to protect election credibility amidst heightened domestic and foreign adversary interest.
